<div style="clear:both;" class=""></div>All statistics correct as of June 15, 2026.</td></tr></tbody></table><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none">International football competition</div>
<p>The <b>2026 FIFA World Cup</b> is the current and 23rd edition of the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup" title="FIFA World Cup">FIFA World Cup</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Quadrennial" class="mw-redirect" title="Quadrennial">quadrennial</a> international men's <a href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">soccer</a> championship contested by the <a href="/wiki/List_of_men%27s_national_association_football_teams" title="List of men's national association football teams">national teams</a> of the member associations of <a href="/wiki/FIFA" title="FIFA">FIFA</a>. The tournament began on June 11 and is scheduled to conclude on July 19, 2026.<sup id="cite_ref-Schedule_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Schedule-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is jointly hosted by sixteen cities: eleven in the United States, three in Mexico, and two in Canada. The tournament is the first FIFA World Cup to be hosted by three nations and the first to include 48 teams, an expansion from the previous 32-team format.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/United_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_bid" title="United 2026 FIFA World Cup bid">United 2026 bid</a> beat a <a href="/wiki/Morocco_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_bid" title="Morocco 2026 FIFA World Cup bid">rival bid by Morocco</a> during a final vote at the <a href="/wiki/68th_FIFA_Congress" title="68th FIFA Congress">68th FIFA Congress</a> in <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a>. It is the first World Cup since <a href="/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2002 FIFA World Cup">2002</a> to be co-hosted by multiple nations. With its past hosting of the <a href="/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1970 FIFA World Cup">1970</a> and <a href="/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1986 FIFA World Cup">1986</a> tournaments, Mexico became the first country to host or co-host the World Cup three times. The United States previously hosted the World Cup in <a href="/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1994 FIFA World Cup">1994</a>. By contrast, it is Canada's first time hosting or co-hosting the tournament. The event is returning to its traditional <a href="/wiki/Northern_Hemisphere" title="Northern Hemisphere">Northern Hemisphere</a> summer schedule after the <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">2022 World Cup</a> in Qatar was uniquely held in November and December.
</p><p>As the host nations, <a href="/wiki/Canada_men%27s_national_soccer_team" title="Canada men's national soccer team">Canada</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mexico_national_football_team" title="Mexico national football team">Mexico</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/United_States_men%27s_national_soccer_team" title="United States men's national soccer team">United States</a> all automatically qualified. <a href="/wiki/Cape_Verde_national_football_team" title="Cape Verde national football team">Cape Verde</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cura%C3%A7ao_national_football_team" title="Curaçao national football team">Curaçao</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jordan_national_football_team" title="Jordan national football team">Jordan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Uzbekistan_national_football_team" title="Uzbekistan national football team">Uzbekistan</a> will all make their World Cup debuts. <a href="/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team" title="Argentina national football team">Argentina</a> is the <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_final" title="2022 FIFA World Cup final">defending champion</a>, having won its third World Cup in 2022.
</p><p>Preparations for the tournament have drawn <a href="/wiki/List_of_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_controversies" title="List of 2026 FIFA World Cup controversies">controversy</a>, particularly over the <a href="/wiki/Immigration_policy_of_the_second_Trump_administration" title="Immigration policy of the second Trump administration">United States's immigration and visa policies</a> affecting qualified teams and their fans, <a href="/wiki/Iran_national_football_team" title="Iran national football team">Iran</a>'s participation during amid an <a href="/wiki/2026_Iran_war" title="2026 Iran war">ongoing war waged by the United States and Israel</a>, and FIFA's use of <a href="/wiki/Dynamic_pricing#Professional_sports" title="Dynamic pricing">dynamic ticket pricing</a>.
</p><p>The first goal of the 2026 FIFA World Cup was scored by <a href="/wiki/Juli%C3%A1n_Qui%C3%B1ones" title="Julián Quiñones">Julián Quiñones</a> of <a href="/wiki/Mexico_national_football_team" title="Mexico national football team">Mexico</a> against <a href="/wiki/South_Africa_national_soccer_team" title="South Africa national soccer team">South Africa</a> in the 9th minute of the opening match of the tournament, held on  June 11, 2026, at the <a href="/wiki/Estadio_Azteca" title="Estadio Azteca">Estadio Azteca</a> in <a href="/wiki/Mexico_City" title="Mexico City">Mexico City</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc">
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Format">Format</h2></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Expansion">Expansion</h3></div>
<p>The idea of expanding the tournament had been suggested as early as 2013 by then <a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a> president <a href="/wiki/Michel_Platini" title="Michel Platini">Michel Platini</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and also in 2016 by FIFA president <a href="/wiki/Gianni_Infantino" title="Gianni Infantino">Gianni Infantino</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Opponents of the proposal argued that the number of matches played was already at an unacceptable level, that the expansion would dilute the quality of the matches,<sup id="cite_ref-auto_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto1_7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto1-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and that the decision was driven by political rather than sporting concerns, accusing Infantino of using the promise of bringing more countries to the World Cup to <a href="/wiki/2016_FIFA_Extraordinary_Congress" title="2016 FIFA Extraordinary Congress">win his election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Starting with this edition, the FIFA World Cup expanded to 48 teams, an increase of 16 teams compared to the previous seven tournaments.<sup id="cite_ref-48teams_9-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48teams-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The teams will be split into twelve groups of four teams, with the top two teams in each group and the eight best third-placed teams progressing to a new round of 32, as approved by the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Council" title="FIFA Council">FIFA Council</a> on March 14, 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-IMC_10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IMC-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This is set to be the first expansion and format change since <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_1998" class="mw-redirect" title="FIFA World Cup 1998">1998</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The total number of matches played will increase from 64 to 104, and the number of matches played by teams reaching the final four will increase from seven to eight. The tournament will last 39 days, an increase from 32 days of the <a href="/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2014 FIFA World Cup">2014</a> and <a href="/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2018 FIFA World Cup">2018</a> tournaments.<sup id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Each team will still play three group matches.<sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The final matchday at club level for players named in the final squads is May 24, 2026; clubs have to release their players by May 25, with exceptions granted to players participating in continental club competition finals up until May 30. The 56 days of the combined rest, release, and tournament periods remain identical to the <a href="/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2010 FIFA World Cup">2010</a>, 2014, and 2018 tournaments.<sup id="cite_ref-IMC_10-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IMC-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Other_expansion_formats_explored">Other expansion formats explored</h4></div>
<p>The expansion to 48 teams had already been approved on January 10, 2017, when it was initially decided that the tournament would include 16 groups of 3 teams, and 80 matches in total, with the top two teams of each group progressing to a round of 32.<sup id="cite_ref-48teams_9-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48teams-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Under this later-superseded format, the maximum number of matches per team would have remained at seven, but each team would have played one fewer group match than before. The tournament would still have been completed within 32 days.<sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This format was initially chosen over three other proposals, ranging from 40 to 48 teams, from 76 to 88 matches, and from one to four minimum matches per team.<sup id="cite_ref-heraldlive_18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-heraldlive-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-yahoo_19-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-yahoo-19"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Critics of this format argued that the use of three-team groups with two teams progressing significantly increased the risk of collusion between teams.<sup id="cite_ref-guyon_21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guyon-21"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This prompted FIFA to suggest that <a href="/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football)" title="Penalty shoot-out (association football)">penalty shootouts</a> may be used to prevent draws in the group stage,<sup id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> although even then some risk of collusion would remain, and a possibility would emerge of teams deliberately losing shootouts to eliminate a rival.<sup id="cite_ref-guyon_21-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guyon-21"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> To address these concerns, FIFA continued considering alternative formats<sup id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> – a process that ended with the 2023 announcement that the format would be 12 groups of 4 teams.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="New_rules">New rules</h3></div>
<p>The 2026 FIFA World Cup introduces several rule changes. In accordance with <a href="/wiki/Laws_of_the_Game_(association_football)" title="Laws of the Game (association football)">IFAB</a>, these are primarily designed to reduce time-wasting. The new rules for the tournament include:
</p>
<ul><li>10-second substitutions: Players being substituted have 10 seconds to exit the pitch, otherwise his replacement must wait for one minute before entering the match.</li>
<li>5-second restarts: A visual 5-second countdown can be shown by the referee for throw-ins and goal kicks in situations of time-wasting. If the ball is not put into play in time, possession is awarded to the opposing team.</li>
<li>Medical treatment: Any player who receives medical attention on the pitch must leave the field and wait for 1 minute before returning to play.</li>
<li>Expanded <a href="/wiki/Video_assistant_referee" title="Video assistant referee"><abbr title="video assistant referee">VAR</abbr></a><span class="sr-only" style="border: 0;   clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); clip-path: polygon(0px 0px, 0px 0px, 0px 0px); height: 1px; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; padding: 0; position: absolute; width: 1px; white-space: nowrap;">Tooltip video assistant referee</span>: VAR can now review and overturn clear mistakes on given second yellow cards, wrongly awarded corner kicks, expanded mistaken identity, and certain attacking fouls.</li>
<li>Mouth-covering red cards: To stop confrontational or insulting behavior hidden from lip-reading, any player who covers his mouth with his hand, arm, or shirt while confronting an opponent will be issued a red card.<sup id="cite_ref-newrules_24-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-newrules-24"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Breaks">Breaks</h3></div>
<p>Cooling or <a href="/wiki/Hydration_break" class="mw-redirect" title="Hydration break">hydration breaks</a> were introduced at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. For the 2026 World Cup, FIFA has introduced mandatory 3-minute hydration <a href="/wiki/Time-out_(sport)" title="Time-out (sport)">breaks in every half for all matches</a>. Broadcasters are permitted to run <a href="/wiki/Television_timeout" title="Television timeout">commercials</a> during these pauses.<sup id="cite_ref-Breaks_25-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Breaks-25"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Host_selection">Host selection</h2></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/United_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_bid" title="United 2026 FIFA World Cup bid">United 2026 FIFA World Cup bid</a> and <a href="/wiki/Morocco_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_bid" title="Morocco 2026 FIFA World Cup bid">Morocco 2026 FIFA World Cup bid</a></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Council" title="FIFA Council">FIFA Council</a> went back and forth between 2013 and 2017 on limitations within hosting rotation based on the continental confederations. Originally, it was set that bids to be host would not be allowed from countries belonging to confederations that hosted the two preceding tournaments. It was temporarily changed to only prohibit countries belonging to the confederation that hosted the previous World Cup from bidding to host the following tournament,<sup id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> before the rule was changed back to its prior state of two World Cups.<sup id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Council" title="FIFA Council">FIFA Council</a> made an exception to potentially grant eligibility to member associations of the confederation of the second-to-last host of the FIFA World Cup in the event that none of the received bids fulfill the strict technical and financial requirements.<sup id="cite_ref-fifacouncil_28-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fifacouncil-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ap-cbc_29-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ap-cbc-29"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In March 2017, FIFA president <a href="/wiki/Gianni_Infantino" title="Gianni Infantino">Gianni Infantino</a> confirmed that "Europe (<a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a>) and Asia (<a href="/wiki/Asian_Football_Confederation" title="Asian Football Confederation">AFC</a>) are excluded from the bidding following the selection of <a href="/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2018 FIFA World Cup">Russia</a> and <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">Qatar</a> in 2018 and 2022 respectively."<sup id="cite_ref-guardian_30-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian-30"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Therefore, the 2026 World Cup could be hosted by one of the remaining four confederations: <a href="/wiki/CONCACAF" title="CONCACAF">CONCACAF</a> (North America; last hosted in <a href="/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1994 FIFA World Cup">1994</a>), <a href="/wiki/Confederation_of_African_Football" title="Confederation of African Football">CAF</a> (Africa; last hosted in <a href="/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2010 FIFA World Cup">2010</a>), <a href="/wiki/CONMEBOL" title="CONMEBOL">CONMEBOL</a> (South America; last hosted in <a href="/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2014 FIFA World Cup">2014</a>), or OFC (Oceania, never hosted before), or potentially by AFC or UEFA in case no bid from the others met the requirements.<sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Co-hosting the FIFA World Cup—which had been banned by FIFA after the <a href="/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2002 FIFA World Cup">2002 World Cup</a>—was approved for the 2026 World Cup, though not limited to a specific number, but instead evaluated on a case-by-case basis. Also for 2026, the FIFA general secretariat, after consultation with the Competitions Committee, had the power to exclude bidders who did not meet the minimum technical requirements to host the competition.<sup id="cite_ref-fifacouncil_28-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fifacouncil-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Canada, Mexico, and the United States had each publicly considered bidding for the tournament separately, but the United joint bid was announced on April 10, 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:3_33-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-33"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In March 2022, <a href="/wiki/Liga_MX" title="Liga MX">Liga MX</a> president <a href="/wiki/Mikel_Arriola" title="Mikel Arriola">Mikel Arriola</a> claimed Mexico's involvement as cohost could have been at risk if the league and the federation had not responded quickly to the <a href="/wiki/Quer%C3%A9taro%E2%80%93Atlas_riot" title="Querétaro–Atlas riot">Querétaro–Atlas riot</a> between rival fans that left 26 spectators injured and resulted in 14 arrests. Arriola said FIFA was "shocked" by the incident but Infantino was satisfied with the sanctions handed down against Querétaro.<sup id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<p>The voting took place on June 13, 2018, during the <a href="/wiki/68th_FIFA_Congress" title="68th FIFA Congress">68th FIFA Congress</a> in <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a>, and it was opened to all 203 eligible members.<sup id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>35<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The United bid won with 134 valid ballots, while the Morocco bid received 65 valid ballots.<sup id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-36"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:3_33-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-33"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Iran voted for neither of the two bids, while Cuba, Slovenia, and Spain abstained from voting. <a href="/wiki/Ghana_Football_Association" title="Ghana Football Association">Ghana</a> was suspended by FIFA due to a corruption scandal and was therefore ineligible to vote.<sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

<p>During the bidding process, 41 cities with 42 existing, fully functional venues with regular tenants (except Montreal) and two venues under construction (Las Vegas and Los Angeles) submitted to be part of the bid (three venues in three cities in Mexico; six venues in six cities in Canada; 35 venues in 32 cities in the United States).<sup id="cite_ref-bids_42-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bids-42"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A first-round elimination cut nine venues and nine cities. A second-round elimination cut an additional nine venues in six cities, while three venues in three cities (<a href="/wiki/Chicago" title="Chicago">Chicago</a>, <a href="/wiki/Minneapolis" title="Minneapolis">Minneapolis</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Vancouver" title="Vancouver">Vancouver</a>) dropped out due to FIFA's unwillingness to discuss financial details.<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> After <a href="/wiki/Montreal" title="Montreal">Montreal</a> dropped out in July 2021 due to lack of provincial funding and support to renovate <a href="/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Montreal)" title="Olympic Stadium (Montreal)">Olympic Stadium</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Vancouver rejoined the bid as a candidate city in April 2022,<sup id="cite_ref-vancouver_candidatecity_45-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vancouver_candidatecity-45"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>45<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> bringing the total number to 24 venues, each in its own city or metropolitan area.<sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On June 16, 2022, the sixteen host cities (two in Canada, three in Mexico, eleven in the United States) were announced by <a href="/wiki/FIFA" title="FIFA">FIFA</a>: Atlanta, Boston, Dallas, Guadalajara, Houston, Kansas City, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Miami, Monterrey, New York/New Jersey, Philadelphia, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, Toronto, and Vancouver.<sup id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>47<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Eight of the sixteen chosen stadiums have permanent <a href="/wiki/Artificial_turf" title="Artificial turf">artificial turf</a> surfaces that are planned to be replaced with grass under the direction of FIFA and a <a href="/wiki/University_of_Tennessee" title="University of Tennessee">University of Tennessee</a>–<a href="/wiki/Michigan_State_University" title="Michigan State University">Michigan State University</a> research team. Depending on the venue's climate, the turf used is either a hybrid of 84% <a href="/wiki/Poa_pratensis" title="Poa pratensis">Kentucky bluegrass</a> and 16% <a href="/wiki/Lolium_perenne" title="Lolium perenne">perennial ryegrass</a> (for cooler temperatures), or <a href="/wiki/Cynodon_dactylon" title="Cynodon dactylon">Bermuda grass</a> (for warmer temperatures).<sup id="cite_ref-utk-fifa_48-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-utk-fifa-48"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>48<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-tsn-henry-26_49-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tsn-henry-26-49"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>49<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-conv-tr-g-s-b-26_50-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-conv-tr-g-s-b-26-50"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>50<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Four venues (Atlanta, Dallas, Houston, and Vancouver) are indoor stadiums that use <a href="/wiki/Retractable_roof" title="Retractable roof">retractable roof</a> systems, all equipped with climate control, while a fifth, Los Angeles, is open-air but has a translucent roof and no climate control.<sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>51<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The host of the <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_final" title="2026 FIFA World Cup final">final match</a>—<a href="/wiki/MetLife_Stadium" title="MetLife Stadium">MetLife Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/East_Rutherford,_New_Jersey" title="East Rutherford, New Jersey">East Rutherford, New Jersey</a>—was announced by FIFA on February 4, 2024.<sup id="cite_ref-ESPN-Schedule_52-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ESPN-Schedule-52"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>52<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Although there are <a href="/wiki/Soccer-specific_stadium" title="Soccer-specific stadium">soccer-specific stadiums</a> in Canada and the United States, the largest dedicated soccer-specific stadium in the United States, <a href="/wiki/Geodis_Park" title="Geodis Park">Geodis Park</a> in <a href="/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee" title="Nashville, Tennessee">Nashville, Tennessee</a>, seats 30,000, which falls short of FIFA's minimum of 40,000 (Toronto's <a href="/wiki/BMO_Field" title="BMO Field">BMO Field</a> is being expanded from 30,000 to 45,500 for this tournament).<sup id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>53<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Stadiums including <a href="/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Stadium" title="Mercedes-Benz Stadium">Mercedes-Benz Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/Atlanta" title="Atlanta">Atlanta</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gillette_Stadium" title="Gillette Stadium">Gillette Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/Foxborough,_Massachusetts" title="Foxborough, Massachusetts">Foxborough, Massachusetts</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Lumen_Field" title="Lumen Field">Lumen Field</a> in <a href="/wiki/Seattle" title="Seattle">Seattle</a> are used by <a href="/wiki/National_Football_League" title="National Football League">National Football League</a> (NFL) and <a href="/wiki/Major_League_Soccer" title="Major League Soccer">Major League Soccer</a> (MLS) teams.<sup id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>54<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Although primarily used for <a href="/wiki/Gridiron_football" title="Gridiron football">gridiron football</a>, with the American stadiums hosting NFL teams and Canada's hosting the <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Football_League" title="Canadian Football League">Canadian Football League</a> (CFL), all of the Canadian and American stadiums have been used on numerous occasions for soccer and are also designed to host that sport.<sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>55<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Mexico_City" title="Mexico City">Mexico City</a> is the only capital of the three host nations chosen as a venue site, with <a href="/wiki/Ottawa" title="Ottawa">Ottawa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C.">Washington, D.C.</a>, joining <a href="/wiki/Bonn" title="Bonn">Bonn</a> (<a href="/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1974 FIFA World Cup">West Germany, 1974</a>) and <a href="/wiki/Tokyo" title="Tokyo">Tokyo</a> (<a href="/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2002 FIFA World Cup">Japan, 2002</a>) as the only capital cities not selected to host World Cup matches. Washington was a host city candidate, but due to the poor state of <a href="/wiki/Northwest_Stadium" title="Northwest Stadium">Northwest Stadium</a>, it combined its bid with nearby <a href="/wiki/Baltimore" title="Baltimore">Baltimore</a>'s, which was unsuccessful. Other cities eliminated from the final hosting list were <a href="/wiki/Cincinnati" title="Cincinnati">Cincinnati</a>, <a href="/wiki/Denver" title="Denver">Denver</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee" title="Nashville, Tennessee">Nashville</a>, <a href="/wiki/Orlando,_Florida" title="Orlando, Florida">Orlando</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Edmonton" title="Edmonton">Edmonton</a>. Ottawa's candidate venue, <a href="/wiki/TD_Place_Stadium" title="TD Place Stadium">TD Place Stadium</a>, was eliminated early on due to insufficient capacity.<sup id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>56<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Though eight of the metropolitan areas hosting games had previously hosted World Cup games (<a href="/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex" title="Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex">Dallas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Greater_Los_Angeles" title="Greater Los Angeles">Los Angeles</a>, <a href="/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area" title="San Francisco Bay Area">San Francisco Bay Area</a>, <a href="/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area" title="New York metropolitan area">New York/New Jersey</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Greater_Boston" title="Greater Boston">Boston</a> in <a href="/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1994 FIFA World Cup">1994</a>; <a href="/wiki/Guadalajara_metropolitan_area" title="Guadalajara metropolitan area">Guadalajara</a> and <a href="/wiki/Greater_Mexico_City" title="Greater Mexico City">Mexico City</a> in both <a href="/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1970 FIFA World Cup">1970</a> and <a href="/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1986 FIFA World Cup">1986</a>; <a href="/wiki/Monterrey_metropolitan_area" title="Monterrey metropolitan area">Monterrey</a> in 1986), <a href="/wiki/Estadio_Azteca" title="Estadio Azteca">Estadio Azteca</a> is the only stadium in this tournament that previously hosted World Cup games, having done so in both 1970 and 1986; none of the stadiums used in the 1994 FIFA World Cup will be used in this tournament.<sup id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>57<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Soldier_Field" title="Soldier Field">Soldier Field</a> in Chicago, the <a href="/wiki/Cotton_Bowl_(stadium)" title="Cotton Bowl (stadium)">Cotton Bowl</a> in Dallas, and the <a href="/wiki/Rose_Bowl_(stadium)" title="Rose Bowl (stadium)">Rose Bowl</a> in <a href="/wiki/Pasadena,_California" title="Pasadena, California">Pasadena</a> (Los Angeles area) were the only stadia in the bidding process to have hosted games in 1994, but none of them were selected.<sup id="cite_ref-bids_42-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bids-42"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Due to FIFA's rules on stadium <a href="/wiki/Naming_rights" title="Naming rights">sponsorships</a>, the venues will use alternative names for the duration of the tournament, shown below in parentheses.<sup id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>58<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FIFA_stadia_59-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FIFA_stadia-59"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>59<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The capacity is based on information published by FIFA.<sup id="cite_ref-FIFA_stadia_59-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FIFA_stadia-59"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>59<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Teams">Teams</h2></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Qualification">Qualification</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification" title="2026 FIFA World Cup qualification">2026 FIFA World Cup qualification</a></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:2026_world_cup_qualification_map.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/2026_world_cup_qualification_map.svg/500px-2026_world_cup_qualification_map.svg.png" decoding="async" width="400" height="176" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/2026_world_cup_qualification_map.svg/960px-2026_world_cup_qualification_map.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="2756" data-file-height="1214"></a><figcaption><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#0000ff; color:white;-webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact;"> </span> Team qualified</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#ffcc00; color:black;-webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact;"> </span> Team eliminated</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#000000; color:white;-webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact;"> </span> Team withdrew or suspended</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#cccccc; color:black;-webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact;"> </span> Not a FIFA member</div></figcaption></figure>
<p>The United Bid personnel anticipated that all three host countries would be awarded automatic berths.<sup id="cite_ref-bid_cities_60-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bid_cities-60"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>60<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On August 31, 2022, FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed that six CONCACAF teams would qualify for the World Cup, with Canada, Mexico, and the United States automatically qualifying as hosts.<sup id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>61<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>62<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This was confirmed by the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Council" title="FIFA Council">FIFA Council</a> on February 14, 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>63<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-64"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>64<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Immediately prior to the 67th <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Congress" title="FIFA Congress">FIFA Congress</a>, the FIFA Council approved the slot allocation in a meeting in <a href="/wiki/Manama" title="Manama">Manama</a>, Bahrain.<sup id="cite_ref-slot_65-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-slot-65"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>65<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-66" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-66"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>66<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This included an intercontinental playoff tournament involving six teams to decide the last two FIFA World Cup spots.<sup id="cite_ref-fifa_council_67-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fifa_council-67"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>67<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The six teams in the playoffs comprised one team from each confederation excluding <a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a>, and one additional team from the confederation of the host countries (<a href="/wiki/CONCACAF" title="CONCACAF">CONCACAF</a>). Two of the teams were seeded based on the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Men%27s_World_Ranking" title="FIFA Men's World Ranking">World Rankings</a>, and they played the winners of two knockout matches between the four unseeded teams for the two <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup" title="FIFA World Cup">FIFA World Cup</a> berths. The four-match tournament was played in Mexico, one of the host countries, and was also used as a test event for the FIFA World Cup.<sup id="cite_ref-slot_65-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-slot-65"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>65<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The ratification of slot allocation also gave the <a href="/wiki/Oceania_Football_Confederation" title="Oceania Football Confederation">OFC</a> a guaranteed berth in the final tournament for the first time: the 2026 FIFA World Cup will be the first tournament in which all six confederations have at least one guaranteed berth and also the first time since the <a href="/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2010 FIFA World Cup">2010 edition</a> in which all confederations have a team qualified for the World Cup finals.<sup id="cite_ref-slot_65-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-slot-65"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>65<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Of the 48 qualified teams, 26 also appeared in the <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">2022 edition</a>. Highlights include:
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Cape_Verde_national_football_team" title="Cape Verde national football team">Cape Verde</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>68<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Cura%C3%A7ao_national_football_team" title="Curaçao national football team">Curaçao</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>A<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:2_70-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-70"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>69<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Jordan_national_football_team" title="Jordan national football team">Jordan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Uzbekistan_national_football_team" title="Uzbekistan national football team">Uzbekistan</a><sup id="cite_ref-71" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-71"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>B<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-72"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>70<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> will all make their World Cup debuts.</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Qatar_national_football_team" title="Qatar national football team">Qatar</a> advanced to the tournament through qualification for the first time, as its only previous appearance was as host in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>71<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/DR_Congo_national_football_team" title="DR Congo national football team">DR Congo</a><sup id="cite_ref-74" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-74"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>C<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Haiti_national_football_team" title="Haiti national football team">Haiti</a> return to the tournament after appearing in their only previous tournament in <a href="/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1974 FIFA World Cup">1974</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_70-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-70"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>69<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>72<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Iraq_national_football_team" title="Iraq national football team">Iraq</a> returns to the tournament after appearing in its only previous tournament in <a href="/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1986 FIFA World Cup">1986</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>73<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Austria_national_football_team" title="Austria national football team">Austria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Norway_national_football_team" title="Norway national football team">Norway</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>74<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Scotland_national_football_team" title="Scotland national football team">Scotland</a> return to the tournament after last appearing in <a href="/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1998 FIFA World Cup">1998</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>75<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Turkey_national_football_team" title="Turkey national football team">Turkey</a> qualified for the first time since finishing third in <a href="/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2002 FIFA World Cup">2002</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-79" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-79"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>76<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team" title="Czech Republic national football team">Czech Republic</a><sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>D<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> qualified for the first time since <a href="/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2006 FIFA World Cup">2006</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>77<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/New_Zealand_men%27s_national_football_team" title="New Zealand men's national football team">New Zealand</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paraguay_national_football_team" title="Paraguay national football team">Paraguay</a>, and <a href="/wiki/South_Africa_national_soccer_team" title="South Africa national soccer team">South Africa</a> (2010 World Cup host) return after last taking part in <a href="/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2010 FIFA World Cup">2010</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>78<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> South Africa achieved its first successful qualifying campaign since <a href="/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2002 FIFA World Cup">2002</a> while New Zealand is the lowest ranked team to qualify, ranked 85th.<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>79<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Algeria_national_football_team" title="Algeria national football team">Algeria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_national_football_team" title="Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team">Bosnia and Herzegovina</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ivory_Coast_national_football_team" title="Ivory Coast national football team">Ivory Coast</a> qualified for the first time since <a href="/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2014 FIFA World Cup">2014</a>. Bosnia achieved its first successful qualification process for a major tournament since the 2014 World Cup.</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Colombia_national_football_team" title="Colombia national football team">Colombia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Egypt_national_football_team" title="Egypt national football team">Egypt</a>, <a href="/wiki/Panama_national_football_team" title="Panama national football team">Panama</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Sweden_men%27s_national_football_team" title="Sweden men's national football team">Sweden</a> return after missing the previous tournament in <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">2022</a>.</li></ul>
<p>Four-time champion <a href="/wiki/Italy_national_football_team" title="Italy national football team">Italy</a> missed out after being defeated in the <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_second_round#Path_A" title="2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round">European playoff final</a> by Bosnia and Herzegovina on <a href="/wiki/Penalty_shootout" class="mw-redirect" title="Penalty shootout">penalties</a>, becoming the first former champion to miss out on three consecutive World Cups;<sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>80<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> as in <a href="/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2018 FIFA World Cup">2018</a> and 2022, Italy was the only former champion that did not qualify. With a <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Men%27s_World_Ranking" title="FIFA Men's World Ranking">FIFA Men's World Ranking</a> of 12, Italy was also the highest-ranking team that did not qualify. <a href="/wiki/Costa_Rica_national_football_team" title="Costa Rica national football team">Costa Rica</a> failed to qualify for the first time since <a href="/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2010 FIFA World Cup">2010</a>, while <a href="/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team" title="Cameroon national football team">Cameroon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Denmark_national_football_team" title="Denmark national football team">Denmark</a>, <a href="/wiki/Poland_national_football_team" title="Poland national football team">Poland</a>, <a href="/wiki/Serbia_national_football_team" title="Serbia national football team">Serbia</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Wales_national_football_team" title="Wales national football team">Wales</a>, all of whom qualified in 2022, did not qualify.<sup id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>81<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Nigeria_national_football_team" title="Nigeria national football team">Nigeria</a>, the 3rd-highest ranked African nation, missed out on qualification for the second straight finals, while in South America, <a href="/wiki/Peru_national_football_team" title="Peru national football team">Peru</a> missed out on their second straight finals and <a href="/wiki/Chile_national_football_team" title="Chile national football team">Chile</a> their third. 
</p><p>The qualified teams, listed by region, with numbers in parentheses indicating final positions in the FIFA Men's World Ranking before the tournament were:<sup id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>82<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Draw">Draw</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_draw" title="2026 FIFA World Cup draw">2026 FIFA World Cup draw</a></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Official_Draw_(54966258098).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Official_Draw_%2854966258098%29.jpg/330px-FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Official_Draw_%2854966258098%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="155" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Official_Draw_%2854966258098%29.jpg/960px-FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Official_Draw_%2854966258098%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3000" data-file-height="1547"></a><figcaption>From left to right, FIFA President <a href="/wiki/Gianni_Infantino" title="Gianni Infantino">Gianni Infantino</a>, US President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a>, Mexican President <a href="/wiki/Claudia_Sheinbaum" title="Claudia Sheinbaum">Claudia Sheinbaum</a> and Canadian Prime Minister <a href="/wiki/Mark_Carney" title="Mark Carney">Mark Carney</a> at the start of the draw.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The draw took place on December 5, 2025, at the <a href="/wiki/Kennedy_Center" title="Kennedy Center">Kennedy Center</a> in <a href="/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C.">Washington, D.C.</a><sup id="cite_ref-94" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-94"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>83<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The draw ceremony began with FIFA presenting the first (and as of 2026<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_FIFA_World_Cup&action=edit" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_FIFA_World_Cup&action=edit">[update]</a></sup> the only) <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_draw" title="2026 FIFA World Cup draw">FIFA Peace Prize</a> to United States president <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Guardian-main_95-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Guardian-main-95"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>84<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> an award which fueled scrutiny and controversy among human rights groups, analysts, and others.<sup id="cite_ref-AJ-Analysis_96-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AJ-Analysis-96"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>85<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Amnesty_97-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Amnesty-97"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>86<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NewHumanitarian_98-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NewHumanitarian-98"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>87<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-99"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>88<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The 48 teams were divided into four pots of 12. Pot 1 consisted of the three hosts and the top nine teams from the November 2025 <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Men%27s_World_Ranking" title="FIFA Men's World Ranking">FIFA Men's World Ranking</a>. Pots 2, 3, and 4 consisted of the remaining teams according to the ranking. The four winners of the <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_second_round" title="2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round">UEFA playoffs</a> and the two winners of the <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(inter-confederation_play-offs)" title="2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (inter-confederation play-offs)">inter-confederation playoffs</a> were not known at the time of the draw and thus were automatically allocated to Pot 4. The 12 groups were randomly formed by selecting one team from each of the four pots. FIFA's "general principle, whenever possible", was that no group had more than one team from the same confederation drawn into it.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>89<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>90<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This principle was applicable to all confederations except UEFA; each group was required to have either one or two UEFA teams drawn into it.
</p><p>The three host nations were pre-allocated to three groups for scheduling purposes. Mexico was placed in Group A and played the opening match of the tournament at <a href="/wiki/Estadio_Azteca" title="Estadio Azteca">Estadio Azteca</a> on June 11. Canada and the United States were placed in Groups B and D, respectively. They played the third and fourth matches of the tournament, respectively, both on June 12.<sup id="cite_ref-Schedule_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Schedule-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>91<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The confederation restriction applied to all three potential winners of the inter-confederation playoffs. FIFA also announced that, "in the interest of ensuring competitive balance", two separate pathways to the semifinals (sides of the knockout bracket) were established. Based on this, the teams ranked first (Spain) and second (Argentina) in the ranking were randomly drawn into groups in opposite pathways, as were the teams ranked third (France) and fourth (England). Therefore, should these pairs of teams win their groups, they will be unable to meet until the final, while all four will be unable to meet until the semifinals.<sup id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-103"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>92<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The draw started with Pot 1 and ended with Pot 4, with each team selected and then allocated into the first available group alphabetically. For the purpose of the match schedule, the Pot 1 teams were automatically drawn into position 1 of each group. For the remaining pots, FIFA established a predetermined pattern to define the position of teams based on their pot and the group they were drawn into.
</p>

<p>Base camps will be used by the 48 national squads to stay and train before and during the World Cup tournament.<sup id="cite_ref-Team_Base_camps_109-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Team_Base_camps-109"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-110"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>95<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>96<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>97<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Similar to the prohibition of naming-rights sponsors that apply to the competition venues, the names of some training facilities were also altered by FIFA.<sup id="cite_ref-113" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-113"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>98<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Squads">Squads</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_squads" title="2026 FIFA World Cup squads">2026 FIFA World Cup squads</a></div>
<p>Before submitting their final squad for the tournament, teams named a provisional squad of between 35 and 55 players one month prior to the tournament. Teams were required to name their final squads by June 2. If a player becomes too injured or ill to prevent his participation in the tournament, he can be replaced by another player from the provisional squad until 24 hours before the team's first match. However, an injured or ill goalkeeper may be replaced by another goalkeeper from the provisional squad at any time during the tournament.<sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>144<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Officiating">Officiating</h2></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_officials" title="2026 FIFA World Cup officials">2026 FIFA World Cup officials</a></div>
<p>On April 9, 2026, <a href="/wiki/FIFA" title="FIFA">FIFA</a> announced the list of 52 referees, 88 assistant referees, and 30 <a href="/wiki/Video_assistant_referee" title="Video assistant referee">video assistant referees</a> for the tournament.<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>145<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>146<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Ceremonies">Ceremonies</h2></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Opening_ceremonies">Opening ceremonies</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_opening_ceremonies" title="2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremonies">2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremonies</a></div>
<p>The tournament is set to feature three opening ceremonies, one for each of the hosts.<sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The opening ceremony in Mexico took place on June 11, 2026, at Estadio Banorte and featured performances by Mexican rock band <a href="/wiki/Man%C3%A1" title="Maná">Maná</a>, Mexican singers <a href="/wiki/Belinda_Peregr%C3%ADn" title="Belinda Peregrín">Belinda</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Lila_Downs" title="Lila Downs">Lila Downs</a>, Mexican cumbia band <a href="/wiki/Los_%C3%81ngeles_Azules" title="Los Ángeles Azules">Los Ángeles Azules</a>, Nigerian singer <a href="/wiki/Burna_Boy" title="Burna Boy">Burna Boy</a>, Colombian singers <a href="/wiki/J_Balvin" title="J Balvin">J Balvin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ryan_Castro" title="Ryan Castro">Ryan Castro</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Shakira" title="Shakira">Shakira</a>, Venezuelan singer <a href="/wiki/Danny_Ocean_(singer)" title="Danny Ocean (singer)">Danny Ocean</a>, Italian tenor <a href="/wiki/Andrea_Bocelli" title="Andrea Bocelli">Andrea Bocelli</a>, and South Korean-American singer <a href="/wiki/Ejae" title="Ejae">Ejae</a> as well as an appearance by Mexican-American actress <a href="/wiki/Salma_Hayek" title="Salma Hayek">Salma Hayek</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>148<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
Mexican singer <a href="/wiki/Alejandro_Fern%C3%A1ndez" title="Alejandro Fernández">Alejandro Fernández</a> performed "<a href="/wiki/Himno_Nacional_Mexicano" title="Himno Nacional Mexicano">Himno Nacional Mexicano</a>" and South African singer <a href="/wiki/Tyla" title="Tyla">Tyla</a> performed the "<a href="/wiki/National_anthem_of_South_Africa" title="National anthem of South Africa">National anthem of South Africa</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>149<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>150<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>151<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The opening ceremony in Canada took place on June 12, 2026, at BMO Field in Toronto and featured performances by Canadian singers <a href="/wiki/Alessia_Cara" title="Alessia Cara">Alessia Cara</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jessie_Reyez" title="Jessie Reyez">Jessie Reyez</a>, <a href="/wiki/Michael_Bubl%C3%A9" title="Michael Bublé">Michael Bublé</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nora_Fatehi" title="Nora Fatehi">Nora Fatehi</a>, and <a href="/wiki/William_Prince_(musician)" title="William Prince (musician)">William Prince</a>, Palestinian singer <a href="/wiki/Elyanna" title="Elyanna">Elyanna</a>, Bangladeshi-American DJ <a href="/w/index.php?title=Sanjoy&action=edit&redlink=1" class="new" title="Sanjoy (page does not exist)">Sanjoy</a>, French singer <a href="/wiki/Vegedream" title="Vegedream">Vegedream</a> as well as an appearance by Canadian-American actor <a href="/wiki/Will_Arnett" title="Will Arnett">Will Arnett</a>. Canadian-American musician <a href="/wiki/Alanis_Morissette" title="Alanis Morissette">Alanis Morissette</a> performed "<a href="/wiki/O_Canada" title="O Canada">O Canada</a>" while Serbian-Canadian violinist Aleksandar Gajić performed "<a href="/wiki/National_anthem_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina" title="National anthem of Bosnia and Herzegovina">Državna himna Bosne i Hercegovine</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>152<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>153<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On the same day, the opening ceremony for the United States took place at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles and featured performances by American singer <a href="/wiki/Katy_Perry" title="Katy Perry">Katy Perry</a>, American rapper <a href="/wiki/Future_(rapper)" title="Future (rapper)">Future</a>, Thai rapper and <a href="/wiki/Blackpink" title="Blackpink">Blackpink</a> member <a href="/wiki/Lisa_(rapper)" title="Lisa (rapper)">Lisa</a>, Brazilian singer <a href="/wiki/Anitta_(singer)" title="Anitta (singer)">Anitta</a>, Nigerian singer <a href="/wiki/Rema_(musician)" title="Rema (musician)">Rema</a>, and South African singer Tyla as well as an appearance by American actor <a href="/wiki/Jason_Sudeikis" title="Jason Sudeikis">Jason Sudeikis</a>. American country duo <a href="/wiki/Dan_%2B_Shay" title="Dan + Shay">Dan + Shay</a> performed "<a href="/wiki/The_Star-Spangled_Banner" title="The Star-Spangled Banner">The Star-Spangled Banner</a>" while Paraguayan soul duo Purahei Soul performed "<a href="/wiki/Paraguayan_National_Anthem" title="Paraguayan National Anthem">Himno Nacional Paraguayo</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>155<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In the days leading up to the tournament, a countdown concert took place in the same cities on June 10. The Toronto concert at <a href="/wiki/Fort_York" title="Fort York">Fort York</a> and <a href="/wiki/The_Bentway" title="The Bentway">The Bentway</a> featured performances by Canadian rock band <a href="/wiki/The_Beaches_(band)" title="The Beaches (band)">The Beaches</a>, Canadian singers <a href="/wiki/Bryan_Adams" title="Bryan Adams">Bryan Adams</a> and Nora Fatehi, Bangladeshi-American DJ Sanjoy, French singer Vegedream, and a special collaboration between Canadian singer <a href="/wiki/AHI_(musician)" title="AHI (musician)">AHI</a> and Haitian rapper <a href="/wiki/Wyclef_Jean" title="Wyclef Jean">Wyclef Jean</a>. The Mexico City concert at <a href="/wiki/Auditorio_Nacional_(Mexico)" title="Auditorio Nacional (Mexico)">Auditorio Nacional</a> featured performances by Mexican cumbia band Los Ángeles Azules, Mexican singer Belinda, Venezuelan-American singer <a href="/wiki/Elena_Rose" title="Elena Rose">Elena Rose</a>, and Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli. The Los Angeles concert at <a href="/wiki/Crypto.com_Arena" title="Crypto.com Arena">Crypto.com Arena</a> featured performances by American electronic music group <a href="/wiki/Major_Lazer" title="Major Lazer">Major Lazer</a>, Nigerian-American singer <a href="/wiki/Davido" title="Davido">Davido</a>, American singer <a href="/wiki/Ava_Max" title="Ava Max">Ava Max</a>, and American rapper <a href="/wiki/Bia_(rapper)" title="Bia (rapper)">Bia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>156<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>157<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>158<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>159<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Independence_Day_ceremonies">Independence Day ceremonies</h3></div>
<p>In addition, two special ceremonies will take place on July 4, 2026, to honor the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Semiquincentennial" title="United States Semiquincentennial">United States Semiquincentennial</a> at <a href="/wiki/Lincoln_Financial_Field" title="Lincoln Financial Field">Lincoln Financial Field</a> in Philadelphia and <a href="/wiki/NRG_Stadium" title="NRG Stadium">NRG Stadium</a> in Houston.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>160<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Match_schedule">Match schedule</h2></div>
<p>The match schedule, without group assignments, was announced on February 4, 2024.<sup id="cite_ref-Schedule_1-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Schedule-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:6_176-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-176"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Q&A_177-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Q&A-177"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>162<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On June 13, 2024, FIFA released an updated schedule, with specific pairings assigned to venues for the knockout stage.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>163<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In addition, group stage matches were assigned to specific groups (though pairings for non-host groups were not assigned to specific matches until after the final draw; thus the group venues were known, but not for which specific pairing each matchday). The full schedule was unveiled in a live broadcast on December 6, 2025, the day after the draw. Group stage pairings were allocated to specific matches, and the kickoff times were confirmed for all fixtures.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>164<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The final match will feature the first-ever <a href="/wiki/Super_Bowl" title="Super Bowl">Super Bowl</a>-style <a href="/wiki/Halftime_show" title="Halftime show">halftime show</a> in FIFA World Cup history. Produced by Global Citizen and curated by <a href="/wiki/Chris_Martin" title="Chris Martin">Chris Martin</a> of <a href="/wiki/Coldplay" title="Coldplay">Coldplay</a>, the performance will co-headline <a href="/wiki/Madonna" title="Madonna">Madonna</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shakira" title="Shakira">Shakira</a>, and <a href="/wiki/BTS" title="BTS">BTS</a> to support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund.<sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The opening match was announced to include Mexico; it took place on June 11, 2026, at the <a href="/wiki/Estadio_Azteca" title="Estadio Azteca">Estadio Azteca</a> in <a href="/wiki/Mexico_City" title="Mexico City">Mexico City</a>. This match included South Africa.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The opening match involving Canada took place on June 12 at <a href="/wiki/BMO_Field" title="BMO Field">BMO Field</a> in <a href="/wiki/Toronto" title="Toronto">Toronto</a>, while the opening match for the United States took place on the same day at <a href="/wiki/SoFi_Stadium" title="SoFi Stadium">SoFi Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/Inglewood,_California" title="Inglewood, California">Inglewood</a>. Each host nation is scheduled to play each of its three matches in the group stage within its own country.<sup id="cite_ref-:6_176-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-176"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium" title="AT&T Stadium">AT&T Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/Arlington,_Texas" title="Arlington, Texas">Arlington</a>, will host the most matches of any venue at the tournament, with nine. <a href="/wiki/MetLife_Stadium" title="MetLife Stadium">MetLife Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/East_Rutherford,_New_Jersey" title="East Rutherford, New Jersey">East Rutherford</a>, will host the <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_final" title="2026 FIFA World Cup final">final</a> on July 19. The United States will host 78 matches, including from the quarterfinal stage onward, while Canada and Mexico will each host 13. Each tournament venue, except for the <a href="/wiki/Estadio_Akron" title="Estadio Akron">Estadio Akron</a>, will host at least one knockout stage fixture.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The match schedule will overlap with the <a href="/wiki/2026_CFL_season" title="2026 CFL season">2026 CFL season</a>, resulting in scheduling conflicts and loss of home games for the <a href="/wiki/Toronto_Argonauts" title="Toronto Argonauts">Toronto Argonauts</a> and <a href="/wiki/BC_Lions" title="BC Lions">BC Lions</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>168<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The match schedule will also affect the <a href="/wiki/2026_Major_League_Baseball_season" title="2026 Major League Baseball season">2026 Major League Baseball season</a> schedules of the <a href="/wiki/Kansas_City_Royals" title="Kansas City Royals">Kansas City Royals</a>, <a href="/wiki/Philadelphia_Phillies" title="Philadelphia Phillies">Philadelphia Phillies</a>, <a href="/wiki/Seattle_Mariners" title="Seattle Mariners">Seattle Mariners</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball)" title="Texas Rangers (baseball)">Texas Rangers</a>, whose home stadiums are located near World Cup venues.<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Host cities were geographically grouped into three regions:<sup id="cite_ref-Schedule_1-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Schedule-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<ul><li>Western Region (Vancouver, Seattle, San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles)</li>
<li>Central Region (Guadalajara, Mexico City, Monterrey, Houston, Dallas, Kansas City)</li>
<li>Eastern Region (Atlanta, Miami, Toronto, Boston, Philadelphia, New York/New Jersey)</li></ul>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Group_stage">Group stage</h2></div>
<p>The group stage will be played from June 11 to 27.<sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>171<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Competing countries were divided into twelve groups of four teams (groups A to L), with teams in each group playing one another in a <a href="/wiki/Round-robin_tournament" title="Round-robin tournament">round-robin</a>. In the group standings, three points are awarded for a win, one for a draw, and none for a loss. Following the conclusion of group play, the top two teams of each group, along with the <a href="#Ranking_of_third-placed_teams">eight best third-placed teams</a> across all groups, will advance to the <a href="#Knockout_stage">knockout stage</a>.
</p><p><i>All times are local.</i>
</p>
<table class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-made-collapsible">
<caption><span class="nowrap"><span class="anchor" id="Tiebreakers"></span> Tie-breaking criteria for group stage ranking</span>
<button type="button" class="mw-collapsible-toggle mw-collapsible-toggle-default" aria-expanded="true" tabindex="0"><span class="mw-collapsible-text">hide</span></button></caption>
<tbody><tr>
<td>The ranking of teams in each group is determined by the points obtained in all group matches. If two or more teams are equal on points, the following criteria are used to determine the ranking:<sup id="cite_ref-regulations_187-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-regulations-187"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
<div><ol style="list-style-type:lower-alpha"><li>Most points obtained in the group matches played between the teams concerned;</li><li>Superior goal difference in the group matches played between the teams concerned;</li><li>Most goals scored in the group matches played between the teams concerned;</li></ol></div>
<p>If, after having applied criteria a to c, teams still had an equal ranking, criteria a to c are reapplied exclusively to the matches between the teams who are still level to determine their final rankings. If this procedure does not lead to a decision, criteria d to h apply.
</p>
<div><ol start="4" style="list-style-type:lower-alpha"><li>Superior goal difference in all group matches;</li><li>Most goals scored in all group matches;</li><li>Highest team conduct ("fair play") score in all group matches (only one deduction can be applied to a player or team coach/official in a single match): <div><ul><li>Yellow card: −1 point;</li><li>Indirect red card (second yellow card): −3 points;</li><li>Direct red card: −4 points;</li><li>Yellow card and direct red card: −5 points;</li></ul></div></li><li>Better position in the most recent <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Men%27s_World_Ranking" title="FIFA Men's World Ranking">FIFA Men's World Ranking</a>;</li><li>Better position in progressively older FIFA Men's World Rankings until teams can be separated.</li></ol></div>
</td></tr></tbody></table>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Group_A">Group A</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_A" title="2026 FIFA World Cup Group A">2026 FIFA World Cup Group A</a></div>
<p>The opening match of the tournament saw the co-host, <a href="/wiki/Mexico_national_football_team" title="Mexico national football team">Mexico</a>, face off against  <a href="/wiki/South_Africa_national_soccer_team" title="South Africa national soccer team">South Africa</a>, as it did first in the <a href="/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2010 FIFA World Cup">2010 FIFA World Cup</a>. Mexico scored within the first 10 minutes by <a href="/wiki/Juli%C3%A1n_Qui%C3%B1ones" title="Julián Quiñones">Julián Quiñones</a>, while <a href="/wiki/Ra%C3%BAl_Jim%C3%A9nez" title="Raúl Jiménez">Raúl Jiménez</a> netted the second goal in the second half, scoring his first World Cup goal. The match also saw straight red cards from South Africa's <a href="/wiki/Sphephelo_Sithole" title="Sphephelo Sithole">Sphephelo Sithole</a> and <a href="/wiki/Themba_Zwane" title="Themba Zwane">Themba Zwane</a> in the second half, while <a href="/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Montes" title="César Montes">César Montes</a> received the match's third straight red card in the second half stoppage time, making it the most red cards in a World Cup opening match in history.<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>173<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On the same day, <a href="/wiki/South_Korea_national_football_team" title="South Korea national football team">South Korea</a> defeated <a href="/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team" title="Czech Republic national football team">Czech Republic</a> 2–1 after going down one by <a href="/wiki/Ladislav_Krej%C4%8D%C3%AD_(footballer,_born_1999)" title="Ladislav Krejčí (footballer, born 1999)">Ladislav Krejčí</a> in the second half, thanks to goals by <a href="/wiki/Hwang_In-beom" title="Hwang In-beom">Hwang In-beom</a> and <a href="/wiki/Oh_Hyeon-gyu" title="Oh Hyeon-gyu">Oh Hyeon-gyu</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>174<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p>
