<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Group_B">Group B</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_B" title="2026 FIFA World Cup Group B">2026 FIFA World Cup Group B</a></div>
<p>Group B saw the second co-host, <a href="/wiki/Canada_men%27s_national_soccer_team" title="Canada men's national soccer team">Canada</a>, open its World Cup campaign against <a href="/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_national_football_team" title="Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team">Bosnia and Herzegovina</a>, where the two teams shared points thanks to the Bosnians' first half goal by <a href="/wiki/Jovo_Luki%C4%87" title="Jovo Lukić">Jovo Lukić</a>, who rose above a Canadian player to power home a header, and Canada's second-half goal by <a href="/wiki/Cyle_Larin" title="Cyle Larin">Cyle Larin</a>, who took only 121 seconds after being substituted on. This saw the co-host's first-ever World Cup points in history.<sup id="cite_ref-:8_196-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:8-196"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>175<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Switzerland_national_football_team" title="Switzerland national football team">Switzerland</a> opened its campaign against <a href="/wiki/Qatar_national_football_team" title="Qatar national football team">Qatar</a> with a <a href="/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football)" title="Penalty kick (association football)">penalty</a> by <a href="/wiki/Breel_Embolo" title="Breel Embolo">Breel Embolo</a> despite offside claims.<sup id="cite_ref-:4_197-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-197"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  However, Switzerland conceded a late equalizer after substitute <a href="/wiki/Miro_Muheim" title="Miro Muheim">Miro Muheim</a> accidentally deflected the ball into the Swiss net, giving Qatar its first-ever World Cup point.<sup id="cite_ref-:4_197-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-197"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Group_C">Group C</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_C" title="2026 FIFA World Cup Group C">2026 FIFA World Cup Group C</a></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team" title="Brazil national football team">Brazil</a> started its campaign against <a href="/wiki/Morocco_national_football_team" title="Morocco national football team">Morocco</a>. The latter took the lead early in the first half with a goal from <a href="/wiki/Ismael_Saibari" title="Ismael Saibari">Ismael Saibari</a>; Brazil responded quickly with a goal from <a href="/wiki/Vin%C3%ADcius_J%C3%BAnior" title="Vinícius Júnior">Vinícius Júnior</a> 11 minutes later. The second half produced no further goals and the two ultimately shared a point apiece.<sup id="cite_ref-205" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-205"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>178<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Meanwhile, <a href="/wiki/Scotland_national_football_team" title="Scotland national football team">Scotland</a> bested <a href="/wiki/Haiti_national_football_team" title="Haiti national football team">Haiti</a> to top the group after the first matchday, with <a href="/wiki/John_McGinn" title="John McGinn">John McGinn</a>'s first half goal proving enough to record Scotland's first World Cup match victory since <a href="/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1990 FIFA World Cup">1990</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-207" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-207"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1011077906">
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Group_D">Group D</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_D" title="2026 FIFA World Cup Group D">2026 FIFA World Cup Group D</a></div><p>The third co-host, the <a href="/wiki/United_States_men%27s_national_soccer_team" title="United States men's national soccer team">United States</a>, faced off against <a href="/wiki/Paraguay_national_football_team" title="Paraguay national football team">Paraguay</a> in its opening match. In the first ten minutes, the United States scored off a deflection from Paraguay's <a href="/wiki/Dami%C3%A1n_Bobadilla" title="Damián Bobadilla">Damián Bobadilla</a>. <a href="/wiki/Folarin_Balogun" title="Folarin Balogun">Folarin Balogun</a> debuted with two goals in the first half, scoring the United States' first World Cup <a href="/wiki/Brace_(association_football)" class="mw-redirect" title="Brace (association football)">brace</a> since <a href="/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1930 FIFA World Cup">1930</a>. In the second half, <a href="/wiki/Maur%C3%ADcio_(footballer,_born_2001)" title="Maurício (footballer, born 2001)">Maurício</a> reduced the deficit for Paraguay, but the United States' <a href="/wiki/Giovanni_Reyna" title="Giovanni Reyna">Giovanni Reyna</a> scored a stoppage-time <a href="/wiki/Curl_(association_football)" title="Curl (association football)"><i>trivela</i></a> to finish proceedings. The co-host scored more goals (four) than it did during the <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">2022 FIFA World Cup</a> (three).<sup id="cite_ref-215" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-215"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>180<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Australia_men%27s_national_soccer_team" title="Australia men's national soccer team">Australia</a> won its opener against <a href="/wiki/Turkey_national_football_team" title="Turkey national football team">Turkey</a> 2–0.  Despite Turkey having possession of the ball for the majority of the game, Australia's <a href="/wiki/Nestory_Irankunda" title="Nestory Irankunda">Nestory Irankunda</a> scored in the first half, and <a href="/wiki/Connor_Metcalfe" title="Connor Metcalfe">Connor Metcalfe</a> in the second.<sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1011077906">

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Group_E">Group E</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_E" title="2026 FIFA World Cup Group E">2026 FIFA World Cup Group E</a></div><p><a href="/wiki/Germany_national_football_team" title="Germany national football team">Germany</a> began its campaign against debutant <a href="/wiki/Cura%C3%A7ao_national_football_team" title="Curaçao national football team">Curaçao</a>. <a href="/wiki/Felix_Nmecha" title="Felix Nmecha">Felix Nmecha</a> scored for the Germans within the first six minutes, but the Curaçaoans scored an equalizer thanks to <a href="/wiki/Livano_Comenencia" title="Livano Comenencia">Livano Comenencia</a>, seeing Curaçao's first ever World Cup goal. The two remained in a stalemate until goals from <a href="/wiki/Nico_Schlotterbeck" title="Nico Schlotterbeck">Nico Schlotterbeck</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jamal_Musiala" title="Jamal Musiala">Jamal Musiala</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nathaniel_Brown_(footballer)" title="Nathaniel Brown (footballer)">Nathaniel Brown</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Deniz_Undav" title="Deniz Undav">Deniz Undav</a>, along with <a href="/wiki/Kai_Havertz" title="Kai Havertz">Kai Havertz’s</a> brace, sealed a 7–1 victory for the Germans.<sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>182<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Amad_Diallo" title="Amad Diallo">Amad Diallo</a> scored a late winner for <a href="/wiki/Ivory_Coast_national_football_team" title="Ivory Coast national football team">Ivory Coast</a>, securing a 1–0 victory over <a href="/wiki/Ecuador_national_football_team" title="Ecuador national football team">Ecuador</a> as the latter failed to capitalize on its chances.<sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>183<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1011077906">

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Group_F">Group F</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_F" title="2026 FIFA World Cup Group F">2026 FIFA World Cup Group F</a></div><p>The <a href="/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team" title="Netherlands national football team">Netherlands</a> faced <a href="/wiki/Japan_national_football_team" title="Japan national football team">Japan</a> in the opener. In the first half, neither team scored.<sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Afterward, the match took a turn when <a href="/wiki/Virgil_van_Dijk" title="Virgil van Dijk">Virgil van Dijk's</a> header sealed the Dutch's opening goal, but <a href="/wiki/Keito_Nakamura" title="Keito Nakamura">Keito Nakamura</a> equalized seven minutes later. <a href="/wiki/Crysencio_Summerville" title="Crysencio Summerville">Crysencio Summerville</a> restored the lead not too long after, but the Netherlands conceded an equalizer after <a href="/wiki/K%C5%8Dki_Ogawa_(footballer)" title="Kōki Ogawa (footballer)">Kōki Ogawa's</a> header bounced off <a href="/wiki/Daichi_Kamada" title="Daichi Kamada">Daichi Kamada</a> into the net right before stoppage time.<sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Between <a href="/wiki/Sweden_men%27s_national_football_team" title="Sweden men's national football team">Sweden</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tunisia_national_football_team" title="Tunisia national football team">Tunisia</a>, the two nations exchanged goals in the first half: two from Swedes <a href="/wiki/Yasin_Ayari" title="Yasin Ayari">Yasin Ayari</a> and <a href="/wiki/Alexander_Isak" title="Alexander Isak">Alexander Isak</a>, and one from Tunisia's <a href="/wiki/Omar_Rekik" title="Omar Rekik">Omar Rekik</a>. In the second half, Tunisia conceded from <a href="/wiki/Viktor_Gy%C3%B6keres" title="Viktor Gyökeres">Viktor Gyökeres</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mattias_Svanberg" title="Mattias Svanberg">Mattias Svanberg</a>, including Ayari's second in stoppage time. Additionally, Svanberg's goal was initially ruled <a href="/wiki/Offside_(association_football)" title="Offside (association football)">offside</a>, but was reinstated after VAR confirmed that Isak had slightly tipped the ball with his foot, eliminating the offside in question.<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1011077906">
</p><table class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;">

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Group_H">Group H</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_H" title="2026 FIFA World Cup Group H">2026 FIFA World Cup Group H</a></div><p><a href="/wiki/Cape_Verde_national_football_team" title="Cape Verde national football team">Cape Verde</a> made its World Cup debut against <a href="/wiki/Spain_national_football_team" title="Spain national football team">Spain</a> and held the heavy favorite to the first goalless draw of the tournament. </p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Knockout_stage">Knockout stage</h2></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage" title="2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage">2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage</a></div>
<p>This is the first tournament with the new round of 32. The knockout stage will be played in a <a href="/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament" title="Single-elimination tournament">single-elimination format</a>, starting with the round of 32 on June 28 and culminating with the <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_final" title="2026 FIFA World Cup final">final</a> on July 19. On the day prior, a <a href="#Match_for_third_place">match for third place</a> will also be played between the two losing semifinalists to determine the third-place team. In the knockout stage, if the scores are level when normal playing time expires, 30 minutes of <a href="/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football" title="Overtime (sports)">extra time</a> will be played. If still tied at the end of extra time, a <a href="/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football)" title="Penalty shoot-out (association football)">penalty shootout</a> will be used to determine the winner.<sup id="cite_ref-regulations_187-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-regulations-187"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Discipline">Discipline</h3></div>
<p>A player or team official is automatically suspended for the next match for the following offenses:<sup id="cite_ref-regulations_187-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-regulations-187"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<ul><li>Receiving a red card (red card suspensions may be extended for serious offenses)</li>
<li>Receiving two yellow cards in the tournament;<sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>Q<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> yellow cards expire after the completion of the group stage and again after the quarterfinals (yellow card suspensions are not carried forward to any other future international matches)<sup id="cite_ref-FIFA_Council_April_28_318-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FIFA_Council_April_28-318"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>189<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li></ul>
<p>During qualification, <a href="/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo" title="Cristiano Ronaldo">Cristiano Ronaldo</a> was sent off for violent conduct in Portugal's penultimate match against the <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland_national_football_team" title="Republic of Ireland national football team">Republic of Ireland</a>, with such an offense typically resulting in a ban of at least two matches. Ronaldo was handed a three-match ban, though the final two matches of the ban were suspended for a one-year probationary period, making him eligible to appear in Portugal's opening World Cup match.<sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>190<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On May 8, 2026, the Bureau of the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Council" title="FIFA Council">FIFA Council</a> amended the tournament regulations so that pending one- or two-match suspensions resulting from an indirect red card, a direct red card for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity, or a direct red card for serious foul play during qualification would no longer be carried forward to the final competition.<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>191<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This exempted Argentina's <a href="/wiki/Nicol%C3%A1s_Otamendi" title="Nicolás Otamendi">Nicolás Otamendi</a>, Ecuador's <a href="/wiki/Mois%C3%A9s_Caicedo" title="Moisés Caicedo">Moisés Caicedo</a>, and Qatar's <a href="/wiki/Tarek_Salman" title="Tarek Salman">Tarek Salman</a> from serving their qualifying-round suspensions during the tournament, with the bans to instead be served in a subsequent competition.<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>192<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The following suspensions will be served during the tournament:

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Awards">Awards</h2></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Prize_money">Prize money</h3></div>
<p>In April 2026, FIFA confirmed the prizes for all participating nations. This edition's total distribution for the tournament will be $871 million, $431 million higher than the prize pool of the <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">previous tournament</a>. In addition to the performance-based prize money, each qualified team will also receive a $10 million qualification payment and a $2.5 million preparation fee before the competition.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>194<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Individual_and_team_awards">Individual and team awards</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards" title="FIFA World Cup awards">FIFA World Cup awards</a></div>
<p>The following awards are to be presented at the end of the tournament.
</p>
<ul><li>Golden Boot: Awarded to the tournament's top goal scorer.</li>
<li>Golden Glove: Awarded to the tournament's best goalkeeper.</li>
<li>Golden Ball: Awarded to the best overall player of the tournament.</li>
<li>FIFA Young Player Award: Awarded to the best overall player of the tournament under the age of 21.</li>
<li>FIFA Fair Play Trophy: Awarded to the team with the best disciplinary record that reached the knockout stage.</li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Marketing">Marketing</h2></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Branding">Branding</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:2026_FIFA_WC_countdown_clock_Paseo_de_la_Reforma.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="A freestanding digital clock with Fifa branding placed on the sidewalk." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/2026_FIFA_WC_countdown_clock_Paseo_de_la_Reforma.jpg/250px-2026_FIFA_WC_countdown_clock_Paseo_de_la_Reforma.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="187" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/2026_FIFA_WC_countdown_clock_Paseo_de_la_Reforma.jpg/500px-2026_FIFA_WC_countdown_clock_Paseo_de_la_Reforma.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3187" data-file-height="2390"></a><figcaption>Countdown clock on <a href="/wiki/Paseo_de_la_Reforma" title="Paseo de la Reforma">Paseo de la Reforma</a>, Mexico City</figcaption></figure>
<p>The official emblem and brand identity was unveiled on May 17, 2023, at the <a href="/wiki/Griffith_Observatory" title="Griffith Observatory">Griffith Observatory</a> in <a href="/wiki/Los_Angeles" title="Los Angeles">Los Angeles</a>, <a href="/wiki/California" title="California">California</a>; its basic form consists of a stacked "26" with an image of the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Trophy" title="FIFA World Cup Trophy">FIFA World Cup Trophy</a> in front of it (marking the first time that the trophy has been depicted in a World Cup emblem as a photo, as opposed to a stylized representation), but it is designed to be adaptable to different backdrops.<sup id="cite_ref-324" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-324"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>195<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:0_325-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-325"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The next day, FIFA unveiled variants of the emblem for each of the host cities, which feature color variants and designs that reflect local landscapes or culture (with the Los Angeles emblem featuring a stylized sun and wave, the Monterrey emblem featuring imagery of the <a href="/wiki/Cerro_de_la_Silla" title="Cerro de la Silla">Cerro de la Silla</a> mountain, and Toronto featuring the city skyline and the <a href="/wiki/CN_Tower" title="CN Tower">CN Tower</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>197<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>198<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Reaction to the logo from the initial unveiling was largely negative, with many feeling that the design was either unfinished or uncreative compared to the emblems of past FIFA World Cup tournaments. By contrast, <a href="/wiki/United_States_men%27s_national_soccer_team" title="United States men's national soccer team">United States national team</a> player <a href="/wiki/Jes%C3%BAs_Ferreira" title="Jesús Ferreira">Jesús Ferreira</a> described the emblem as "beautiful".<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>199<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:0_325-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-325"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>200<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:WorldCup2026lposter.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/WorldCup2026lposter.jpg/250px-WorldCup2026lposter.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="244" style="--mw-file-upright: 0.75" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/9/94/WorldCup2026lposter.jpg 2x" data-file-width="279" data-file-height="358"></a><figcaption>Official poster</figcaption></figure>
<p>In March and April 2025, FIFA unveiled a set of 16 posters representing each of the 2026 World Cup host cities. The posters, designed by local artists, were intended to reflect the "distinct identity and heritage" of each host city.<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>201<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>202<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On March 3, 2026, the official poster was unveiled. For the first time, three artists combined their skills and artistic styles to create the official poster: Carson Ting (Canada), Minerva GM (Mexico), and Hank Willis Thomas (United States).<sup id="cite_ref-Official_posters_332-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Official_posters-332"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>203<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Broadcasting_rights">Broadcasting rights</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_broadcasting_rights" title="2026 FIFA World Cup broadcasting rights">2026 FIFA World Cup broadcasting rights</a></div>
<p>On February 12, 2015, FIFA renewed the United States and Canadian broadcasting rights contracts for <a href="/wiki/Fox_Sports_(United_States)" title="Fox Sports (United States)">Fox Sports</a> (US English), <a href="/wiki/Telemundo_Deportes" title="Telemundo Deportes">Telemundo Deportes</a> (US Spanish), and <a href="/wiki/Bell_Media" title="Bell Media">Bell Media</a> (Canada) to cover the 2026 World Cup, without accepting any other bids. A report in <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times" title="The New York Times">The New York Times</a></i> asserted that this extension was intended as compensation for the rescheduling of the <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">2022 World Cup</a> to November–December rather than its traditional June–July scheduling, as it created considerable conflicts with <a href="/wiki/Major_professional_sports_leagues_in_the_United_States_and_Canada" title="Major professional sports leagues in the United States and Canada">major professional sports leagues</a> that are normally in their offseasons during the World Cup.<sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>204<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>205<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-cangloberights_335-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cangloberights-335"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>206<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:TSN_Jack_Poole_Broadcast_Studio_(2026)_closeup.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/TSN_Jack_Poole_Broadcast_Studio_%282026%29_closeup.jpg/250px-TSN_Jack_Poole_Broadcast_Studio_%282026%29_closeup.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/TSN_Jack_Poole_Broadcast_Studio_%282026%29_closeup.jpg/500px-TSN_Jack_Poole_Broadcast_Studio_%282026%29_closeup.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="2687"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Bell_Media" title="Bell Media">Bell Media</a> broadcast studio located at <a href="/wiki/Jack_Poole_Plaza" title="Jack Poole Plaza">Jack Poole Plaza</a> in Vancouver. <a href="/wiki/The_Sports_Network" title="The Sports Network">TSN</a> is the primary broadcaster, while select matches are on <a href="/wiki/CTV_Television_Network" title="CTV Television Network">CTV</a> and <a href="/wiki/Crave_(streaming_service)" title="Crave (streaming service)">Crave</a> in Canada.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/International_Broadcast_Centre" title="International Broadcast Centre">International Broadcast Center</a> (IBC) will be located at the <a href="/wiki/Kay_Bailey_Hutchison_Convention_Center" title="Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center">Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center</a> in <a href="/wiki/Dallas" title="Dallas">Dallas</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>207<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>208<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>209<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Bell Media constructed a broadcast studio at <a href="/wiki/Jack_Poole_Plaza" title="Jack Poole Plaza">Jack Poole Plaza</a> in Vancouver for the tournament (mirroring an arrangement used by Fox during the <a href="/wiki/2015_FIFA_Women%27s_World_Cup" title="2015 FIFA Women's World Cup">2015 FIFA Women's World Cup</a>), which will operate through the final match played in Vancouver on July 11.<sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>210<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On January 8, 2026, FIFA signed a deal to make <a href="/wiki/TikTok" title="TikTok">TikTok</a> a "preferred platform" for World Cup video content. As part of the agreement, broadcasters may stream parts of matches at a dedicated hub on the TikTok app.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>211<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> FIFA then made a similar "preferred platform" deal with <a href="/wiki/YouTube" title="YouTube">YouTube</a> on March 17, allowing broadcasters to stream select matches in full on their respective YouTube channels, as well as stream the first 10 minutes of every match on the platform as "an appetizer encouraging young fans then to watch on traditional channels".<sup id="cite_ref-341" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-341"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>212<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It was later confirmed that YouTube had extended this deal with FIFA and <a href="/wiki/Caz%C3%A9TV" title="CazéTV">CazéTV</a> to show all tournament matches for free in Brazil.<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>213<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>214<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Advertising">Advertising</h3></div>
<p>On May 7, 2026, <a href="/wiki/Adidas" title="Adidas">Adidas</a> released <i>Backyard Legends: the Greatest Football Story Ever Told</i>, a 5-minute short film.<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>247<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>248<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On June 4, 2026, <a href="/wiki/Nike,_Inc." title="Nike, Inc.">Nike</a> released <i>Rip The Script</i>, a 6-minute short film.<sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>249<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>250<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="FIFA_fan_festivals">FIFA fan festivals</h3></div>
<p>FIFA will stage <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Fan_Festival" title="FIFA Fan Festival">fan festivals</a> in cities across the host nations, featuring matches on giant screens and live entertainment.<sup id="cite_ref-NBCNY_380-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NBCNY-380"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>251<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Among the confirmed fan fest locations are <a href="/wiki/Liberty_State_Park" title="Liberty State Park">Liberty State Park</a> in <a href="/wiki/Jersey_City,_New_Jersey" title="Jersey City, New Jersey">Jersey City</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-NBCNY_380-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NBCNY-380"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>251<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Fairmount_Park" title="Fairmount Park">Fairmount Park</a> in <a href="/wiki/Philadelphia" title="Philadelphia">Philadelphia</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>252<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Fort_York" title="Fort York">Fort York</a> and <a href="/wiki/The_Bentway" title="The Bentway">The Bentway</a> in <a href="/wiki/Toronto" title="Toronto">Toronto</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-382" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-382"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>253<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Centennial_Olympic_Park" title="Centennial Olympic Park">Centennial Olympic Park</a> in <a href="/wiki/Atlanta" title="Atlanta">Atlanta</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-fifa-atl-fan-fest-cenn_383-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fifa-atl-fan-fest-cenn-383"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>254<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/East_Downtown_Houston" title="East Downtown Houston">East Downtown Houston</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-384" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-384"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>255<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Tickets">Tickets</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_controversies#Ticket_prices" title="List of 2026 FIFA World Cup controversies">List of 2026 FIFA World Cup controversies § Ticket prices</a></div>
<p>Ticket prices for the 2026 FIFA World Cup initially ranged from $60 for group stage matches to $6,730 for the final—largely increased from the USD equivalent of $69 to $1,607 in the <a href="/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup" title="2022 FIFA World Cup">2022 FIFA World Cup</a>. However, in September 2025, FIFA confirmed it would use <a href="/wiki/Dynamic_pricing" title="Dynamic pricing">dynamic pricing</a> for tickets for the first time, following the practice used in the <a href="/wiki/2025_FIFA_Club_World_Cup" title="2025 FIFA Club World Cup">2025 FIFA Club World Cup</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_385-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-385"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>256<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Hospitality seats were made available in April 2025 via FIFA's ticket partner for the event.<sup id="cite_ref-386" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-386"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>257<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>An initial draw period for non-hospitality seats occurred between September 10–19, 2025, limited to <a href="/wiki/Visa_Inc." title="Visa Inc.">Visa</a> cardholders. A second phase ran from October 27–31, and a third phase started after the final draw of teams on December 5. Sales are capped at four tickets per person per match, and no person is able to purchase more than 40 tickets for the overall tournament. FIFA's official resale platform went live on October 2, 2025.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_385-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-385"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>256<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-387" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-387"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>258<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>A final "last-minute" sales phase reopened on April 22, 2026, approximately 50 days before the start of the tournament, with tickets for all 104 matches made available on a first-come, first-served basis. By that stage, more than five million tickets had been sold out of an expected total exceeding six million, with additional tickets scheduled to be released in phases up to the final, subject to availability.<sup id="cite_ref-Reuters042226_388-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters042226-388"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>259<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Every city hosting the World Cup in the United States has passed a law stating that ticket sales to World Cup events are exempt from state and local sales taxes.<sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>260<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>261<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>262<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Merchandise">Merchandise</h3></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Video_games">Video games</h4></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_video_games#2026_FIFA_World_Cup" title="FIFA World Cup video games">FIFA World Cup video games § 2026 FIFA World Cup</a></div>
<p>On October 2, 2025, FIFA announced the video game <i><a href="/wiki/FIFA_Heroes" title="FIFA Heroes">FIFA Heroes</a></i>, scheduled for release in 2026 on <a href="/wiki/Android_(operating_system)" title="Android (operating system)">Android</a>, <a href="/wiki/IOS" title="IOS">iOS</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nintendo_Switch" title="Nintendo Switch">Nintendo Switch</a>, <a href="/wiki/PlayStation" title="PlayStation">PlayStation</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Xbox" title="Xbox">Xbox</a> platforms.<sup id="cite_ref-392" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-392"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>263<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In May 2026, the <i><a href="/wiki/Football_Manager_26" title="Football Manager 26">Football Manager 26</a></i> video game also announced the addition of licensed 2026 FIFA World Cup content.<sup id="cite_ref-393" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-393"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>264<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In December 2025, <a href="/wiki/Netflix" title="Netflix">Netflix</a> announced a new simulation-type game featuring the World Cup, produced by Delphi Interactive and Refactor Games.<sup id="cite_ref-394" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-394"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>265<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-395" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-395"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>266<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In May 2026, it was announced the Netflix-published game would be titled "<i>FIFA World Cup – Launch Edition</i>" and would be released in June 2026.<sup id="cite_ref-:7_396-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-396"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>267<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In the same May 2026 announcement, FIFA also confirmed that they would adopt a non-exclusive "Digital Football" ecosystem, with games of various genres adopting the FIFA license. Alongside the new World Cup game, were mentioned <i>FIFA Heroes</i>, <i>FIFA Rivals, <a href="/wiki/List_of_Roblox_games" title="List of Roblox games">FIFA Super Soccer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Football_Manager" title="Football Manager">Football Manager</a>, <a href="/wiki/EFootball" title="EFootball">eFootball</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Rocket_League" title="Rocket League">Rocket League</a>,</i> with more games joining the ecosystem in the following months.<sup id="cite_ref-:7_396-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-396"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>267<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-397" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-397"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>268<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Other_products">Other products</h4></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Panini_Group" title="Panini Group">Panini</a> sticker albums were again announced for the 2026 World Cup. Due to the expansion of the tournament, each pack now contains seven stickers as opposed to the usual 5. In the United States and Canada, a set of 12 stickers was reserved for stickers that could only be obtained from Coca-Cola bottles, with each bottle containing a sticker printed inside the label.<sup id="cite_ref-398" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-398"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>269<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In May 2026, it was announced that the 2026 World Cup would be Panini's second-to-last tournament with a sticker album, after FIFA announced that <a href="/wiki/Fanatics,_Inc." title="Fanatics, Inc.">Fanatics</a> (via their <a href="/wiki/Topps" title="Topps">Topps</a> brand) would distribute collectables for FIFA tournaments from 2031.<sup id="cite_ref-399" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-399"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>270<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In conjunction with the tournament, <a href="/wiki/The_Lego_Group" title="The Lego Group">the Lego Group</a> released a series of officially licensed FIFA World Cup 2026-themed construction sets. The collection included models of the FIFA World Cup Trophy, the official tournament emblem, a brick-built <a href="/wiki/Adidas_Trionda" title="Adidas Trionda">Adidas Trionda</a> football containing a miniature stadium, and player-focused sets based on footballers <a href="/wiki/Lionel_Messi" title="Lionel Messi">Lionel Messi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo" title="Cristiano Ronaldo">Cristiano Ronaldo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kylian_Mbapp%C3%A9" title="Kylian Mbappé">Kylian Mbappé</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Vin%C3%ADcius_J%C3%BAnior" title="Vinícius Júnior">Vinícius Júnior</a>. Several sets featured hidden references to the players' careers, alternative display poses, and commemorative World Cup-themed designs.<sup id="cite_ref-400" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-400"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>271<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-401" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-401"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>272<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> To promote the product line, Lego organized FIFA World Cup 2026-themed activations in several markets, including a football festival and pop-up experience in <a href="/wiki/Singapore" title="Singapore">Singapore</a>. The events featured interactive football challenges, football-themed Lego builds, displays of player-inspired models, and promotional giveaways tied to the World Cup collection.<sup id="cite_ref-402" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-402"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>273<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-403" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-403"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>274<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Maple,_Zayu_and_Clutch" title="Maple, Zayu and Clutch">Maple, Zayu and Clutch</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_official_mascots" title="List of FIFA World Cup official mascots">List of FIFA World Cup official mascots</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Mascots_small.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Refer to caption." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/7/77/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Mascots_small.jpg/250px-2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Mascots_small.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="162" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/77/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Mascots_small.jpg 2x" data-file-width="288" data-file-height="187"></a><figcaption>The tournament mascots: Maple the Moose, Zayu the Jaguar, and Clutch the Bald Eagle</figcaption></figure>
<p>The official mascots of the tournament were revealed on September 25, 2025, and are <a href="/wiki/Maple,_Zayu_and_Clutch" title="Maple, Zayu and Clutch">Maple, Zayu and Clutch</a>. Maple is a <a href="/wiki/Moose" title="Moose">moose</a>, Zayu is a <a href="/wiki/Jaguar" title="Jaguar">jaguar</a>, and Clutch is a <a href="/wiki/Bald_eagle" title="Bald eagle">bald eagle</a>, representing Canada, Mexico, and the United States, respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-404" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-404"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>275<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> They were designed to reflect the cultural heritage of their respective countries.<sup id="cite_ref-405" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-405"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>276<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Match_ball">Match ball</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Adidas_Trionda" title="Adidas Trionda">Adidas Trionda</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_official_match_balls" title="List of FIFA World Cup official match balls">List of FIFA World Cup official match balls</a></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Draw_Reception_(54972841852).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="The match ball displayed on a stand." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Draw_Reception_%2854972841852%29.jpg/250px-FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Draw_Reception_%2854972841852%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="242" height="161" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Draw_Reception_%2854972841852%29.jpg/500px-FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Draw_Reception_%2854972841852%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5985" data-file-height="3990"></a><figcaption>Adidas Trionda, the match ball</figcaption></figure>
<p>On May 2, 2025, reports surfaced that the match ball would be called <a href="/wiki/Adidas_Trionda" title="Adidas Trionda">Adidas Trionda</a>. The design features red, green, and blue (the three colors representing Canada, Mexico, and the United States, respectively, and also featured on the host countries' flags), as well as a white wave connecting each of the colors, hence the name using the <a href="/wiki/Spanish_language" title="Spanish language">Spanish</a> words for three (tri) and wave (onda).<sup id="cite_ref-406" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-406"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>277<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The design also features the national symbols of the three host countries (a <a href="/wiki/Maple_leaf" title="Maple leaf">maple leaf</a> for Canada, a <a href="/wiki/Golden_eagle#canadensis" title="Golden eagle">golden eagle</a> for Mexico, and a <a href="/wiki/Five-pointed_star" title="Five-pointed star">five-pointed star</a> for the United States) as well as gold embellishments to represent the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Trophy" title="FIFA World Cup Trophy">World Cup Trophy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-407" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-407"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>278<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Music">Music</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_2026_Official_Album" class="mw-redirect" title="FIFA World Cup 2026 Official Album">FIFA World Cup 2026 Official Album</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_songs_and_anthems" title="List of FIFA World Cup songs and anthems">List of FIFA World Cup songs and anthems</a></div>
<p>The tournament's official instrumental theme music was composed by Zachary Aaron Golden; throughout March 2025, FIFA released remixes of the theme for each host city by local producers, including Bombon (Houston), <a href="/wiki/Dan_the_Automator" title="Dan the Automator">Dan the Automator</a> (San Francisco), Mr. NaisGai (Miami), <a href="/wiki/Take_a_Daytrip" title="Take a Daytrip">Take a Daytrip</a> (New York/New Jersey), <a href="/wiki/Sango_(musician)" title="Sango (musician)">Sango</a> (Seattle), <a href="/wiki/Dallas_Austin" title="Dallas Austin">Dallas Austin</a> (Atlanta), <a href="/wiki/Mexican_Institute_of_Sound" title="Mexican Institute of Sound">Mexican Institute of Sound</a> (Mexico City),  <a href="/wiki/Hill_Kourkoutis" title="Hill Kourkoutis">Hill Kourkoutis</a> (Toronto), Ben Zakharenko and Dayvin (Boston), Grayson Repp (Vancouver), <a href="/wiki/Tech_N9ne" title="Tech N9ne">Tech N9ne</a> (Kansas City), <a href="/wiki/Toy_Selectah" title="Toy Selectah">Toy Selectah</a> (Monterrey), <a href="/wiki/DJ_Jazzy_Jeff" title="DJ Jazzy Jeff">DJ Jazzy Jeff</a> (Philadelphia), DJ Flict (Los Angeles), Bautista (Guadalajara), and <a href="/wiki/Tre_Nagella" title="Tre Nagella">Tre Nagella</a> (Dallas).<sup id="cite_ref-408" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-408"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>279<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-409" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-409"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>280<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The Vancouver version incorporates the traditional welcome songs of the <a href="/wiki/Musqueam_First_Nation" title="Musqueam First Nation">Musqueam</a>, <a href="/wiki/Squamish_Nation" title="Squamish Nation">Squamish</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Tsleil-Waututh_First_Nation" title="Tsleil-Waututh First Nation">Tsleil-Waututh</a> First Nations communities.<sup id="cite_ref-410" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-410"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>281<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The official song "<a href="/wiki/Dai_Dai" title="Dai Dai">Dai Dai</a>" by Colombian singer <a href="/wiki/Shakira" title="Shakira">Shakira</a> and Nigerian singer <a href="/wiki/Burna_Boy" title="Burna Boy">Burna Boy</a> was released on May 15, 2026,<sup id="cite_ref-411" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-411"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>282<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> followed by the official anthem "<a href="/wiki/DNA_(More_Than_a_Game)" title="DNA (More Than a Game)">DNA (More Than a Game)</a>" by French producer <a href="/wiki/David_Guetta" title="David Guetta">David Guetta</a>, featuring Italian tenor <a href="/wiki/Andrea_Bocelli" title="Andrea Bocelli">Andrea Bocelli</a>, South Korean-American singer <a href="/wiki/Ejae" title="Ejae">Ejae</a>, and American rapper <a href="/wiki/Megan_Thee_Stallion" title="Megan Thee Stallion">Megan Thee Stallion</a>, on June 10, 2026,.<sup id="cite_ref-412" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-412"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>283<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p><p>The official soundtrack album was released on June 5, 2026, with its first single "<a href="/wiki/Lighter_(Jelly_Roll_and_Car%C3%ADn_Le%C3%B3n_song)" title="Lighter (Jelly Roll and Carín León song)">Lighter</a>" by <a href="/wiki/Jelly_Roll_(singer)" title="Jelly Roll (singer)">Jelly Roll</a> and <a href="/wiki/Car%C3%ADn_Le%C3%B3n" title="Carín León">Carín León</a> having been released on March 20, 2026; the song had garnered a mixed reception from listeners and critics, with some having falsely assumed that it was meant to be the tournament's official song before "Dai Dai" was released.<sup id="cite_ref-Conversation_413-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Conversation-413"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>284<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-414" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-414"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>285<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:02_415-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-415"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>286<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Controversies">Controversies</h2></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/List_of_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_controversies" title="List of 2026 FIFA World Cup controversies">List of 2026 FIFA World Cup controversies</a></div>
<p>Criticism of the tournament has centered on United States immigration and visa policies under the <a href="/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump" title="Second presidency of Donald Trump">Trump administration</a>, the participation of Iran amid <a href="/wiki/2026_Iran_war" title="2026 Iran war">an ongoing war waged by the United States and Israel</a>, FIFA's ticket pricing, and labor, safety, and transit issues in host cities. Escalating <a href="/wiki/Mexican_drug_war" title="Mexican drug war">drug cartel violence in Mexico</a> has also fueled security concerns for the tournament, prompting the Mexican government to announce the deployment of nearly 100,000 security personnel to protect fans.<sup id="cite_ref-416" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-416"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>287<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-417" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-417"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>288<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some commentators have characterized the tournament as a form of <a href="/wiki/Sportswashing" title="Sportswashing">sportswashing</a>.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2026)">citation needed</span></a></i>]</sup>
</p><p>A 2025 travel ban and its December expansion barred ordinary citizens of Haiti, Iran, Ivory Coast, and Senegal from obtaining visas to attend matches, though players, team staff, and their immediate relatives were exempted.<sup id="cite_ref-418" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-418"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>289<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A visa bond policy requiring deposits of up to $15,000 from fans of five African qualified nations was suspended in May 2026 for ticket holders.<sup id="cite_ref-419" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-419"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>290<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Somali referee <a href="/wiki/Omar_Abdulkadir_Artan" title="Omar Abdulkadir Artan">Omar Abdulkadir Artan</a> was denied entry to the United States in June 2026 despite holding a valid visa, and FIFA removed him from its roster.<sup id="cite_ref-420" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-420"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>291<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Homeland Security officials also said that customs processing could be halted at airports in <a href="/wiki/Sanctuary_city" title="Sanctuary city">sanctuary host cities</a> and that <a href="/wiki/United_States_Immigration_and_Customs_Enforcement" title="United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement">ICE</a> personnel may be present at matches; workers at <a href="/wiki/SoFi_Stadium" title="SoFi Stadium">SoFi Stadium</a> authorized a strike over pay and immigration enforcement concerns before reaching a settlement days ahead of the venue's first match.<sup id="cite_ref-421" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-421"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>292<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-422" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-422"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>293<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Iran_at_the_FIFA_World_Cup" title="Iran at the FIFA World Cup">Iran's participation</a> was in question after America's attacks against Iran. The <a href="/wiki/Football_Federation_Islamic_Republic_of_Iran" title="Football Federation Islamic Republic of Iran">Football Federation of Iran</a> warned to boycott the December 2025 draw after its president was denied a US visa, and America's attacks against Iran prompted Iranian officials to request that the United States be removed as host. The Iranian team relocated its base camp from Arizona to <a href="/wiki/Tijuana" title="Tijuana">Tijuana</a>, received US visas ten days before its opening match, and saw its fan ticket allocation revoked days before the tournament began.<sup id="cite_ref-423" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-423"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>294<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-424" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-424"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>295<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Commentators have argued that the political context surrounding the tournament undermines FIFA's "Football Unites the World" message.<sup id="cite_ref-425" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-425"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>296<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-426" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-426"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>297<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Upon the team's arrival at their training base in Tijuana, Mexico, players wore gold-colored lapel pins bearing the number "168" to honor the victims of the <a href="/wiki/2026_Minab_school_attack" title="2026 Minab school attack">2026 Minab school attack</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-427" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-427"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>298<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Iran and <a href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egypt</a>'s football associations urged FIFA to prevent <a href="/wiki/LGBTQ_movements" title="LGBTQ movements">LGBTQ</a>-related activities linked to the Seattle match, which had been designated a "<a href="/wiki/Pride_Night#FIFA_World_Cup" title="Pride Night">Pride Match</a>" by local organizers.<sup id="cite_ref-428" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-428"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>299<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>FIFA's first use of <a href="/wiki/Dynamic_pricing" title="Dynamic pricing">dynamic pricing</a> for World Cup tickets drew criticism from fans, players, and United States lawmakers over affordability, with prices for the final reaching $11,000 and exceeding $30,000 for premium seats.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_385-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-385"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>256<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The lack of public transit access at several United States venues was also criticized, with round-trip rail fares to <a href="/wiki/MetLife_Stadium" title="MetLife Stadium">MetLife Stadium</a> briefly raised from $13 to $150 and officials closing pedestrian routes to the stadium.<sup id="cite_ref-429" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-429"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>300<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Wolfe_430-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wolfe-430"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>301<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The tournament's environmental impact also drew significant criticism. An independent June 2026 study by carbon accounting firm Greenly estimated the event's total <a href="/wiki/Carbon_footprint" title="Carbon footprint">carbon footprint</a> as equivalent to 7.8 million metric tons of CO₂, more than double the official emissions reported for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. While utilizing existing stadiums limited infrastructure emissions to just 3% of the total, the vast geographical distribution of matches across three North American countries caused spectator and team transit to account for 87.8% of the tournament's overall carbon footprint.<sup id="cite_ref-431" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-431"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>302<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>While the opening match was played in a full stadium, the second match showed thousands of empty seats, again raising concerns about high ticket prices. In an official statement regarding the empty seats, FIFA said this was due to "several ticketed fans standing in concourses rather than staying in their assigned seats".<sup id="cite_ref-432" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-432"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>303<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-433" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-433"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>304<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This statement drew scrutiny, even more so when thousands of empty seats were visible again during the first match played by host nation Canada.<sup id="cite_ref-434" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-434"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>305<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
